  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived

  Three things are happening at once:

      price-sensitive SMB accounts

    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  carry over.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

I am verifying exactly those two, because they are the load-bearing evidence for my chosen action and both are compressed summaries whose original effect sizes, populations, and durations I cannot see -- memory_31 is also the oldest record here (day 12), so its 'durable lift' claim deserves a source check before I lean on it. I am deliberately not verifying memory_73 because I am not choosing promotional pricing: the competitor's entry pricing creates real pressure to discount, but the inherited record already shows the 40% SMB discount bought signup (+31%) and revenue (+18%) at the cost of churn (+12%), and it was explicitly logged as a one-off and not standard. Trading retention for signups is the wrong move against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, and matching a competitor on price is a fight we would be starting from a weaker position. Referral incentives (memory_57) are sound but apply to established customers and do nothing for the activation/onboarding decline that is actually bleeding. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is a different funnel and does not touch the SMB segment under attack. Activation messaging (memory_91) is my second choice and the most likely follow-up, but it nudges accounts that already reached the product, whereas the onboarding fix widens the pool that gets there at all; if onboarding is the upstream constraint, messaging alone treats the symptom.
